ntlpanel

Nighttime lights to analysis-ready panels for econometrics.

ntlpanel turns nighttime lights rasters into balanced unit-by-period panels. Every observation records how much of the unit was actually observed. The steps that usually happen silently in a script become explicit and recorded:

  • Sensor continuity. NOAA ended Suomi NPP data delivery on 2 November 2026. ntl_splice() puts Suomi NPP (VNP46) and NOAA-20 (VJ146) on one scale and reports level shifts per unit, optionally per calendar month.
  • Coverage. ntl_extract() reports share_valid, share_masked and mean_obs for each unit and period, and keeps “dark” (0) separate from “unobserved” (NA). ntl_gapfill() applies a documented rule to high-latitude summer gaps and flags the cells at risk.
  • Units and design. ntl_crosswalk() moves official statistics between boundary vintages, for example Kazakhstan’s 2022 regions. ntl_exposure() assigns distance rings and first-treatment dates for staggered difference-in-differences designs.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("iskakovs/ntlpanel")
# or: remotes::install_github("iskakovs/ntlpanel")

The package depends on terra, sf, exactextractr, httr2 and hdf5r. Black Marble .h5 files are read with hdf5r rather than through GDAL, so tile orientation does not depend on the GDAL version.

Quick start (offline, synthetic data) 

library(ntlpanel)
ex <- ntl_example()                               # synthetic files + polygons

m    <- ntl_files(ex$dir, "eog_vnl_monthly")      # manifest of local files
long <- ntl_extract(m, ex$units_old, id_col = "district", min_obs = 2)
sp   <- ntl_splice(long, from = "eog_vnl_monthly_npp", to = "eog_vnl_monthly_j01")
ntl_splice_report(sp)                             # level shift per district

p <- ntl_panel(sp, min_share_valid = 0.5)         # balanced, log1p outcome, t index
p <- ntl_gapfill(p, rule = "interp", units = ex$units_old, lat_threshold = 49)

e <- ntl_exposure(ex$units_old, ex$sites, rings = c(50, 100, 200),
                  id_col = "district", site_time_col = "start")

Real data: Black Marble for Kazakhstan 

# One-off: put your NASA Earthdata token in ~/.Renviron as EARTHDATA_TOKEN=...
regions <- sf::st_read("kz_adm1_2022.gpkg")
ntl_tiles(regions)                                # h22-h26 x v03-v04

m_snpp <- ntl_fetch("VNP46A4", aoi = regions, start = 2014, end = 2025)
m_j01  <- ntl_fetch("VJ146A4", aoi = regions, start = 2018, end = 2025)
long   <- ntl_extract(rbind(m_snpp, m_j01), regions, id_col = "region")
sp     <- ntl_splice(long, from = "VNP46A4", to = "VJ146A4")
p      <- ntl_panel(sp)

Downloads go to a temporary folder unless you set a permanent one with NTLPANEL_CACHE in ~/.Renviron (see ?ntl_cache_dir). For monthly data, fetch and extract one year at a time and call ntl_cache_clear() in between. A monthly tile is about 50-130 MB.

Functions

Step Functions
Find data ntl_sources(), ntl_tiles(), ntl_available()
Get data ntl_fetch() (LAADS: VNP46A3/A4, VJ146A3/A4), ntl_files() (EOG VNL, harmonized series, local .h5)
Read and mask ntl_read(), ntl_read_bm(), ntl_mask()
Extract ntl_extract(), ntl_aggregate()
Panel ntl_splice(), ntl_splice_report(), ntl_panel(), ntl_gapfill()
Design ntl_exposure(), ntl_crosswalk(), ntl_apply_crosswalk()
Utilities ntl_cache_dir(), ntl_cache_info(), ntl_cache_clear(), ntl_token(), ntl_example()

Supported products

id What Access
VNP46A3, VNP46A4 Black Marble monthly/annual, Suomi NPP (to Oct 2026) ntl_fetch(), token
VJ146A3, VJ146A4 Black Marble monthly/annual, NOAA-20 ntl_fetch(), token
eog_vnl_monthly, eog_vnl_annual EOG VIIRS Nighttime Lights (npp, j01) with cf_cvg coverage free EOG account, then ntl_files()
dmsp_viirs_li Li et al. (2020) harmonized DMSP-VIIRS, DN scale figshare, ntl_files()
viirs_like_chen Chen et al. (2021) extended VIIRS-like series Harvard Dataverse, ntl_files()
world_nightlights_regan Regan et al. corrected 1992-2023 series GitHub, ntl_files()

Related packages

ntlpanel builds on existing tools rather than replacing them:

Package What it does How ntlpanel differs
blackmarbler (CRAN, World Bank) Downloads Black Marble tiles from LAADS, mosaics them and computes zonal statistics Also reads the NOAA-20 VJ146 products (blackmarbler accepted only Suomi NPP product ids at the time of writing). Adds per-observation coverage diagnostics, cross-sensor splicing, gap rules, balanced panels and boundary crosswalks. Use blackmarbler for the daily products (VNP46A1/A2), which ntlpanel does not cover.
nightlightstats (GitHub) DMSP and VIIRS statistics per GADM region Covers Black Marble and EOG products with coverage counts, and makes panels with any boundaries
Rnightlights DMSP/VIIRS download and zonal statistics Archived on CRAN since 2019
rgee General interface to Google Earth Engine through Python No Python or Earth Engine account needed; focused on nighttime lights panels
exactextractr, terra, sf Raster and vector building blocks ntlpanel uses them for reading, masking and exact zonal statistics

Citation

Run citation("ntlpanel") for the citation of the package. Please also cite the data products you use (see the url column of ntl_sources()).

Contributing

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.md. Never paste your NASA Earthdata token into an issue.

Status and validation

Version 0.1.0.9000 passes R CMD check and its test suite, which runs offline on synthetic rasters, HDF5 fixtures and mocked LAADS responses. Two parts have not yet been run against live data:

  1. Downloads. Authenticated downloads in ntl_fetch(). The URL layout and listing format were checked against the live archive, and the whole download path is tested with mocked responses.
  2. Tile orientation. Orientation with real Black Marble files. Tiles are read with hdf5r (GDAL versions disagree about their row order) and assumed north-up, as in the product specification.

Run system.file("scripts", "validate_splice_kz.R", package = "ntlpanel") first. It checks orientation on a known city and measures the Suomi NPP to NOAA-20 level shift across Kazakhstan’s regions and calendar months.

Roadmap

  • Optional Google Earth Engine back-end for server-side zonal statistics.
  • NOAA-21 products once they are available on LAADS.
  • Network distances in ntl_exposure() (via dodgr).
  • H3 grid helpers built on h3o.
